name: staging-points
status: Team parking rule (Sun Nov 15); the app computes its own staging point at runtime with the same rule
source: Derived from HiRISE 1 m DTM slope and roughness (NASA/JPL/University of Arizona)
caveats: Parking limits are a team decision, not NASA flight rules; NASA sets only the maximum walk back to the rover.
Straight-line walks; walk_km is ground distance on the Mars sphere, not path length over the relief.
Max slope on the walk includes isolated 1 m DTM spikes; check the slope overlay before trusting a single high value.
Not ground-truthed: no rover has operated in Arcadia Planitia.

assumptions: Rover parking: no 1 m slope over 5° in the square; a site with no such square falls back to 10°, flagged slope_fallback (team decision; Apollo 15 Mission Report §9.8.3: LRV roll instability approached on 15° slopes).
Rover parking roughness ≤ 0.25 m RMS on 5 m cells (team decision; LRV ground clearance 36 cm, NASA NSSDC). The 1 m DTM cannot see single rocks.
Each 10 m cell takes the worst (max) slope and roughness inside it; a spot needs a 4 × 4 block of parkable cells (40 × 40 m).

Walk-back ≤ 2 km straight-line ground distance on the Mars sphere (config.yaml walk_back_max_km); spots closer than 25 m to the POI are excluded (team decision after Apollo 17 Station 7, rover ~25 m from the boulder; NASA sets only the maximum).
Walk path = straight line to the POI on the 1 m slope; the suit limit is 20° (config.yaml slope_max_deg). Real walks would detour around steep sections.
Rank by walk_km × (1 + 10 × share of the walk ≥ 20°); alternatives at least 250 m apart.
Slope and roughness come from the 1 m HiRISE DTM (vertical precision ~tens of cm); sub-metre rocks need the 0.25 m imagery.
